# `passportsim endpoint`

Open, describe or close an instance's USB Serial/JTAG endpoints for esptool and idf.py.

| MCP tool | Scenario step | macOS | Windows | Browser |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `passport_endpoint` | none | yes | yes | no |

## Synopsis

```text
passportsim endpoint [instance] [--auto-download] [--clock <CLOCK>] [--close] [--pty] [--tcp] [--json <@file|->]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Form | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auto_download` | `--auto-download` | `boolean` | no | Reset to download on a raw SYNC. |
| `clock` | `--clock <CLOCK>` | `"endpoint"` \| `"agent"` | no | Who drives time (endpoint). |
| `close` | `--close` | `boolean` | no | Close the endpoints. |
| `instance` | `<instance>` | `string` | no | Instance id. |
| `pty` | `--pty` | `boolean` | no | Open a pty (macOS, data only). |
| `tcp` | `--tcp` | `boolean` | no | Open the TCP endpoint on 127.0.0.1. |

A nested object or array is passed as one JSON document with `--json @<file>` or `--json -`; it has no flag of its own.

## Errors

`E_USAGE` (1), `E_STATE` (2), `E_LEASE` (6), `E_HOST_UNSUPPORTED` (19). What each means: [errors.md](../errors.md).

## Examples

### Serve the only instance for esptool over RFC 2217

```sh
passportsim endpoint --json - <<'JSON'
{
  "tcp": true
}
JSON
```

```powershell
@'
{
  "tcp": true
}
'@ | passportsim endpoint --json -
```

### Close the endpoints of p1

```sh
passportsim endpoint --json - <<'JSON'
{
  "close": true,
  "instance": "p1"
}
JSON
```

```powershell
@'
{
  "close": true,
  "instance": "p1"
}
'@ | passportsim endpoint --json -
```
